summary:
French Guiana stands under the national framework of France. Identity documents, the criminal code, anti-discrimination law and marriage law operate here as in metropolitan France, with no separate local statute on gender identity.

French law does not criminalise trans status or gender expression. Same-sex sexual activity in private was decriminalised by the Penal Code of 1791, retained in the Penal Code of 1810, and that position extends to French Guiana.

Legal gender recognition has been available since 1 January 2017 under the law of 18 November 2016. Change of gender marker requires an application to a court and is granted without surgery, sterilisation, psychiatric certificate or medical diagnosis. Change of first name is handled separately at the registry office.

Discrimination on the ground of sexual identity has been prohibited since July 2012. The term in Penal Code article 225-1 was replaced by gender identity on 18 November 2016. The Labour Code prohibits exclusion from recruitment, internships, training or employment and discriminatory sanctions or dismissal on the ground of gender identity.

Since 2017 transphobia constitutes an aggravating circumstance for any crime punishable by imprisonment under French law applicable in French Guiana.

Trans women in France whose detention placement follows legal gender face a legal gray area in prison allocation. The national preventive mechanism found in its opinion of 25 May 2021 that serious violations persist in French places of deprivation of liberty. Both findings apply in French Guiana as a jurisdiction applying French detention law.

Gender-affirming surgery performed in France was legalised in 1979. Specialised trans healthcare in French Guiana remains limited by remoteness, with extended waiting times and inequitable access by location reported at national level in a 2022 ILGA-Europe report.

One overview of French Guiana reported societal transphobia and cultural taboos that discourage visibility and reporting.

Police-identified victims of homophobic and transphobic attacks and insults in France numbered around 1,380 in 2018 and around 1,870 in 2019, a rise of 36 percent reported on 16 May 2020.

Same-sex marriage has been legal in all overseas departments and territories including French Guiana since the 2013 marriage-equality law, following civil solidarity pacts available since 1999. Pride events are held in French Guiana. One travel guide rated French Guiana Very Safe for LGBTQ+ visitors and described a small scene anchored in Cayenne with no listed venues.

Conversion therapy is banned under the law published on 1 February 2022, following Senate passage on 7 December 2020 and National Assembly concurrence on 25 January 2022. The offence carries two years imprisonment and a fine of 30,000 euros.
tangentialFactors:
Legal change of gender was refused for decades in France. The European Court of Human Rights judgment in B. v France in 1992 required reform. A bill was approved by the Senate on 6 November 2015 and by the National Assembly on 24 May 2016, 12 July 2016 and 12 October 2016, ruled constitutional on 17 November 2016 and signed on 18 November 2016.

France declassified gender dysphoria as a mental illness by decree in 2010, the first country to do so. Transgender rights organisations stated that beyond the announcement nothing changed in practice.

The 2022 ILGA-Europe report found lack of self-determination in the French system and recommended informed consent and self-determination. The National Academy of Medicine described increased demand as an epidemic-like phenomenon and a primarily social problem and advised extreme caution, without changing actual practice.

Sexual-orientation discrimination in employment, housing and public and private goods and services was banned in 1985. The law of 31 December 2004 made homophobic injury, defamation, insult, incitement to hatred, violence or discrimination punishable by a fine of 45,000 euros and 12 months imprisonment, amended the Press Law of 29 July 1881, created the Haute autorite, and increased penalties where assault or murder was motivated by sexual orientation.

The age of consent was equalised at 15 on 4 August 1982, removing the prior discriminatory provision for homosexual relations.
localsOnly:
Transsexualism remains listed under ALD 31 with treatment funded by Securite Sociale for residents.

A March 2019 instruction requires higher-education institutions in France, applicable in French Guiana, to use a transgender student's preferred name on student cards and examination forms.

Transgender individuals may serve openly in the French Armed Forces.

Late-2024 guidelines from the French Society of Pediatric Endocrinology recommend puberty blockers from at least Tanner stage 2 with calcium and vitamin D supplementation.

The Senate passed a bill in May 2024 to ban medical transition under age 18. The Macron government opposed the bill. No update in the National Assembly was recorded after 23 July 2024.

In 2022 a controversy arose around DILCRAH after its scientific committee president was found to belong to The Little Mermaid Observatory, a group that called gender-affirming healthcare mutilation. One member resigned and the president stepped away.
